additional_context:
[Council feedback on the previous definition]
From model_reviewer:
- authoring_response.proposed_definition.kinematic_profile.primary_joint_actions[2] (scapulothoracic_joint/retraction): Scapular retraction is in the definition as a full-weight action, so the trapezius transverse part (1.0), rhomboid major (0.9) and rhomboid minor (0.7) become primary movers, and latissimus dorsi and the ascending trapezius pick up synergist credit. The source cue ('pull shoulder blades together' after the bar passes the knees) is a brief lockout adjustment, and the assumptions call it 'a minor action'. The frames show the arms hanging with the bar carried by hip and knee extension. The coefficients contradict the stated intent and overstate upper-back work relative to the glutes, hamstrings and quadriceps. Suggested correction: Mark the scapulothoracic retraction action as emphasis 'assist' (0.4 x table weight), so the rhomboids and transverse trapezius drop to synergist or lower, or remove it and rely on scapular_retraction_stability for the isometric hold. Keep it only if the lockout retraction is a deliberate part of the movement.
[End of council feedback]

assumptions: The axle is treated as a standard barbell deadlift with a bilateral stance, ignoring the over/under grip choice because it does not change the joint actions.
Hip extension and knee extension are the primary load-moving actions.
The cue to pull the shoulder blades together after the bar passes the knees is a brief lockout adjustment, so scapular retraction is marked as assist and not as a primary action.
The spine stays braced and arched, so the back is credited through anti_flexion_spine and not through lumbar extension.
Ankle plantarflexion contributes little to the pull and is omitted.
The bar is held in the hands, so grip is a demand.
The big breath before the pull is treated as bracing, so intra_abdominal_pressure is included.
The reviewer feedback is applied: retraction is demoted to assist and no separate scapular retraction stability demand is added.
classification_reasons: Both frames show a bilateral, two-handed barbell pull from the floor, with a hip-hinged start and an upright standing finish.
Hip extension and knee extension move the load, and the schema vocabulary covers both.
The instructions describe a conventional stance at hip width with the bar over the feet, so the joint actions are unambiguous.

instructions: Approach the bar so that it is centered over your feet. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the bar at shoulder width, allowing your shoulder blades to protract. Typically, you would use an over/under grip.

With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees until your shins contact the bar. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward.
After the bar passes the knees, aggressively pull the bar back, pulling your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward into the bar.
Lower the bar by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.
